text:
Seattle is 9-5-1 and sitting in a playoff conversation it hasn't fully earned. The Kraken have taken only 45% of the expected goals, both overall and at five on five, but they have scored 52 goals on 42.1 expected, nearly 10 more than their chances suggest. By chance quality they deserved about 14 points; they have 19.

The finishing has a face. Berkly Catton, 20, stretched his point streak to seven games in Wednesday's 2-1 overtime win over Calgary, per Alison Lukan, and his line with Shane Wright and Kaapo Kakko has played 105 minutes together while breaking even on chances. That is a real sign for a young core. The Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann line, at 39% of the expected goals, is the one getting buried.

Now the worry. Both goalies have hit a wall at the same time: Philipp Grubauer at .863 over his last five starts, Joey Daccord at .865. Daccord did post plus-2.3 goals saved above expected in that Calgary win, which is the kind of night that can restart a goalie.

Our simulations put Seattle's playoff odds at 41%, with a projected 88 points. If the shooting cools before the goaltending warms up, that number moves the wrong way quickly. If both swing back together, this team is more interesting than its shot share.
headline: Winning on finishing, worried in net
